page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, with the page number at the left. Below it: three centred italic question lines with short answers, a rule, the division title and subtitle, a centred italic question, and a paragraph opening with a woodcut initial. No marginal notes. The catchword "utranq;" sits at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.head: Quis fuit primus & ultimus Rex Ro-manorum?
main_text.p: Romulus fuit primus : ultimus Tarquinius Su-perbus.
main_text.head: Quis fuit primus Imperator Romanus?
main_text.p: Julius Cæsar, quem secutus est Augustus.
main_text.head: Quis fuit primus Imperator Constan-tinopolitanus?
main_text.p: Constantinus Magnus : ultimus fuit Constantinus Palæologus, sub quo Constantinopolim Turcæ ceperunt. •
Lecturus tractationem Historiarum pleniorem videat Chronica Philippi Melanchthonis, quæ D. Doctor Pezelius teutonicè reddidit : Et Martyrolo-gium Fochsi. •
Hastenus est de Historia dictum : Sequitur de Ru-dimentis juris.
main_text.head: DE RUDIMENTIS IURIS.

head.i: Quibus rebus Imperatorem decoratum esse oportet?

main_text.p: IMPERATORIAM Majestatem non solùm armis decoratam, sed etiam legibus oportet esse armatam, ut utrunque tempus, & bellorum & pacis, rectè possit gubernari. In princip.procem.instit.
Fuit : ipse enim inquit §.1.in procem.inst. Quorum

page.notes: The woodcut initial I is read as the first letter of "IMPERATORIAM". The "•" marks after "ceperunt." and "Fochsi." are printer's ornaments and are kept. The question lines are underlined in the print; the underlining is not transcribed. The catchword "utranq;" is printed at the lower right and is not part of the running text.
